description: Defects planted into a staged copy of the fixture to ask one mechanical question of a candidate test suite: does it go red? The fixture itself ships correct, because mutation analysis requires a green baseline and a suite that cannot run cannot be scored. Each defect is an exact-string edit, so applying one is deterministic and reviewable in a diff.

defects.title: POST /quotes accepts zero or negative weight_grams
defects.find:
if raw_weight <= 0:
        raise QuoteRequestError("weight_grams", "weight_grams must be positive")
defects.rationale: Dropping the lower bound quotes a -500g parcel at the zone base rate and a 0g parcel at the same price as a 1g one. The ceiling check above it still passes review, which is exactly why a suite that only tests the happy path and the upper bound walks straight past this.

defects.title: Heavy surcharge applied above the threshold instead of at it
defects.rationale: A parcel weighing exactly the threshold loses its surcharge. Only a test that pins the boundary itself, rather than a value comfortably either side of it, notices.

defects.title: Express multiplier applied before the heavy surcharge
defects.rationale: Reordering only changes the price of a parcel that is both heavy and express, so a suite that tests the two features separately stays green.

defects.title: Part-kilogram parcels round down instead of up
defects.rationale: Every parcel under a kilogram is quoted at the bare base rate. A suite whose weights all land on exact kilogram boundaries cannot see it.
